sections.h2: Routes for selling a Waxahachie house
sections.html:
Three practical paths exist for a Waxahachie owner: list with a broker, sell privately to someone you know, or accept an investor's cash offer. Your choice turns on the repair work the house needs and the day you need the funds.

Waxahachie is the seat of Ellis County, on Interstate 35E and U.S. Highway 287, about thirty miles south of Dallas. Shoppers often hold a house here up against homes nearer Dallas and weigh the drive, so mention highway access whenever you talk about the property.

  • Listing pays off for a sound home if you can live through showings and an appraisal.
  • A private sale skips marketing but still needs a signed deed and a closing agent.
  • Investors fit best with deferred repairs, tenants, probate questions or a hard deadline.

The town was laid out in August 1850 as the county seat and earned the nickname Gingerbread City for the Victorian carpentry on homes built before 1900. About 300 Waxahachie structures are on the federal historic register, including the red sandstone and granite courthouse on the square. A yearly Gingerbread Trail tour of Victorian homes keeps the old architecture in view.

A house in a historic pocket near the square can draw buyers who like period detail, and it can also carry older wiring, plumbing and foundations that an inspection will flag. Tour your own property the way a buyer would, and sort what you see into two columns. Charm goes in one: wood trim, porches, original windows. Trouble goes in the other: failing roofing, settling piers. Comparing the columns shows whether repairs before listing are worth it or whether selling as is is simpler. Photographs of both columns help when you explain the house to a buyer.

Newer subdivisions out toward the highways sit in a different market. The buyer pool there is mostly commuters and families, and the repair list is usually shorter. Ask a local agent or appraiser which category your street falls into before you set an asking price.

sections.h2: Student and rental housing near campuses
sections.html:
Waxahachie grew on cotton and rail, and education added another layer. Trinity University operated in town from 1902 to 1942, Southwestern Bible Institute took over the grounds in 1943, and Navarro College has a branch here. Those institutions explain the clusters of older rental and student housing near campus areas.

The town hosts the Scarborough Renaissance Faire and a Christmas parade and tour of homes, which bring visitors each year. Some sellers time a listing around those events so more people see the street. An investor looks at the house itself, so timing matters less for a cash sale.

sections.h2: Permits for work before a sale
sections.html:
Selling needs no permit, though repair work beforehand may need one from the Permitting Division of the city's Building and Community Services Department. The city runs an online Citizen Self-Service portal for applications, payments, inspection scheduling and plan review. Separate submittal guides cover fences, residential remodels, accessory structures, swimming pools, irrigation and certificates of occupancy. Construction fees are in Chapter 11 of the City Code of Ordinances.

Did an earlier owner add a room, deck or pool? Find out whether the permit was closed. Open or missing permits tend to surface once a buyer's financing is underway, and fixing them before you list costs less than fixing them under contract. Ask the Permitting Division what a closeout would involve, and budget time for an inspection visit.

sections.h2: Tax bills and dates at closing
sections.html:
Ellis County channels bill the taxes on a Waxahachie house, and at closing the year's bill is normally divided between buyer and seller.

Ellis County tax dates
DateWhat happens
October 1Collection period begins and bills are mailed
January 31Last day to pay before the delinquency date
February 1Penalty and interest begin on unpaid taxes
April 30Last day to file an exemption application at the Ellis Appraisal District
May 15Last day to file a protest with the appraisal district
July 1Unpaid accounts move to the tax attorneys, who may add up to 20 percent

Each year's tax lien attaches January 1, so the buyer's closing agent will want any unpaid bill cleared. The county tax office, at 302 N. Monroe Street in Waxahachie, can give a payoff figure for a specific account. Bring the account number from your latest statement and your photo ID to speed that along.

A seller who has claimed a homestead exemption loses it at the sale, and the buyer applies for their own. School districts must give a $140,000 homestead exemption, and an additional $60,000 applies to older or disabled owners. A buyer who closes after January 1 may be able to claim it for the rest of that year if the prior owner did not.

  • Ellis County Clerk staff record the deed, since that office keeps the land records for everything inside the county line.
  • A notary or other authorized officer must witness the signature.
  • The fee schedule charges $5.00 up front with $4.00 added per further page, plus smaller records fees.

The title company needs your government photo ID, the property's legal description and any loan payoff statement. With those in hand, the deed is drafted right the first time. After funding, the company sends the deed to the clerk, and you get a recorded copy for your files.

If your Waxahachie loan is behind, the house is sold at auction on a first Tuesday after the notice has been out for three weeks. Selling before that date can avoid the auction. Check the loan paperwork and ask the county clerk where notices are filed.

Call the lender and a housing counselor right away. A cash buyer can often close within the time left, and a closing before auction day can pay off the loan and leave you any remaining equity. The sooner you start, the more choices you keep.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Waxahachie house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. State law sets no repair duty ahead of a sale, and a cash buyer can purchase a house without any repairs done. Open permits or code issues should still be settled or disclosed, and unpaid taxes or recorded liens will come up during title work.

faqs.q: Which office handles deeds for a Waxahachie property?
faqs.a: Ellis County Clerk staff record deeds, because Texas keeps deed records county by county. The clerk checks that the deed is signed and acknowledged before accepting it.

faqs.q: When are Ellis County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Statements arrive about October 1, with payment due by January 31. Late charges begin February 1, and on July 1 the county hands what remains to its tax attorneys.

faqs.q: Does the age of a Waxahachie house affect a sale?
faqs.a: It can. Many houses near the square date from before 1900, and buyers of those homes may ask for inspections of wiring, plumbing and the foundation. Newer subdivision homes usually raise fewer questions.

faqs.q: What if my Waxahachie house is facing foreclosure?
faqs.a: Contact the lender and a housing counselor right away. A Texas auction takes place on the month's first Tuesday after a sale notice has been posted at the courthouse and lodged with the clerk three weeks earlier. A closing before that day can pay off the loan.
